header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Start: 16:30 PDT
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Evan Zhao (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Chiron CTO), Priya Nair (Chiron SRE), Sam Torres (Chiron Product)
Recording: enabled
Notes: demo focused on Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost-attribution and optimization playbook
summary: Redwood AE + SE walked Chiron through the Console's per-route usage analytics, cost decomposition, and suggested optimization levers (batching, KV caching, quantization recommendations). Customer is evaluating Redwood for a pilot to reduce inference spend and improve latency predictability for two main routes: clinical-summarization and patient-chat. Security questions (SOC2, KMS) surfaced and next steps include a 48-hour perf run and security deep dive.
topics: Console: per-route dashboards; route-level cost decomposition; prefix/KV cache; batching and autoscaling; dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs; security (SOC2, KMS, SSO); pilot scope and success metrics
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hi everyone, thanks for the time. Quick intro — I'm Maya, I'm the AE working with you, Evan's our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Jordan (CTO): Good, thanks. Ready to see the console.
[00:11] Evan (SE): Great, I'll share my screen and jump into the per-route view. bear with me while I load the demo tenant.
[00:25] Speaker 2 (Priya?): Ok, perfect. We mainly want to see cost per route and where the hot tokens are coming from. Our infra team is getting hit by the clinical-summarization costs.
[00:37] Evan (SE): Understood. Alright sharing now — this is the Redwood Console home, top-left is our overall usage timeline, then we'll zoom into Routes.
[00:45] Evan (SE): So this Routes table shows all active endpoints; you can filter by model, region, and by SLO tag, we often ask customers to tag production vs canary. here is your clinical-summarization route, see the spikes?
[01:02] Sam (Product): yes, that's the one. Can you show the breakdown by token type?
[01:08] Evan (SE): Yep, click into the route and there's the per-token breakdown: input vs output tokens, cached hits, batching efficiency, and token-level latency distribution. this chart is showing an average 280ms p99 for that route during peak.
[01:22] Jordan (CTO): 280ms p99 — that's okay but costs are climbing. Where is most of the spend coming from?
[01:29] Evan (SE): Click cost decomposition, you'll see cost split by model compute, memory thermal — sorry memory stick — and infra overhead like cross-region egress. The biggest line item here is model inference compute for the long-context calls. Also note KV cash miss rate is about 85% for this route so you're not getting prefix cache benefit.
[01:49] Priya (SRE): Wait did you say KV cash? we turned on caching with the reference prompt, I thought that should be working.
[01:54] Evan (SE): Right so I think what's happening is the prompt canonicalization isn't aligning; we show the canonicalization compatibility score here — about 0.4 — so a lot of prompts vary slightly and miss the cache. We can show a quick example of how to normalize.
[02:08] Maya (AE): Also worth noting that batching policy is set to conservative here — see concurrency threshold is low, which increases per-token cost. We usually recommend increasing batch window for async summarization routes.
[02:20] Jordan (CTO): If we increase batching window will latency degrade for live chats? that's our second route, patient-chat, which needs low latency.
[02:29] Evan (SE): Good question. Redwood allows per-route policies — you can set patient-chat to aggressive low-latency (small batch sizes, reserved capacity) while setting clinical-summarization to high-throughput batching. The console's route policy link shows fallback model variants and autoscale thresholds.
[02:44] Sam (Product): Show me the cost delta between hosted and dedicated for that summarization route.
[02:50] Evan (SE): On the same route view toggle to 'deployment economics' — here's redwood-hosted vs dedicated vs private. The chart is an estimate based on your token mix and latency SLO. For your traffic profile, dedicated with gpus quantized to 4-bit plus prefix cache hits looks ~37% cheaper at steady state, but needs a commit.
[03:10] Jordan (CTO): Commit is hard for us unless we have a predictable SLO. How do we test that?
[03:15] Evan (SE): We propose a 48-hour perf run using your sample traffic routed to our sandbox dedicated nodes. That will show steady-state throughput, p95/p99 tail, and measured cost. We also instrument the console to show token-level attribution and model variant fallbacks during the run.
[03:30] Priya (SRE): Security — we need to know about KMS and key rotation, also audit logs. We have to prove keys never leave our KMS.
[03:38] Maya (AE): Absolutely. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; for Hosted we use envelope encryption but can integrate with your KMS for BYOK. We'll send the SOC2 and ISO docs; Evan can schedule a security deep dive with your security team.
[03:50] Speaker 1 (Jordan?): Ok please share those docs. Also what about SSO and RBAC? we need role separation for engineer vs analyst.
[03:58] Evan (SE): SSO via SAML is supported, and the Console supports granular RBAC — routes can be tagged with team ownership and who can deploy rollouts. We can demo that in a follow up.
[04:08] Sam (Product): Walk me through a concrete optimization playbook for the summarization route — like a checklist.
[04:15] Evan (SE): Sure — step one: canonicalize prompts to increase prefix cache hits, step two: enable progressive batching (increase batch window during off-peak), step three: switch to a quantized variant of the model we validated, step four: reserve dedicated capacity for steady traffic or use burstable reserved with autoscale, step five: add a fallback policy to a cheaper variant during overload. The Console has a 'suggested optimizations' view that will auto-generate these suggestions and expected cost savings.
[04:45] Priya (SRE): For prompt canonicalization, do we have a tool or is that manual?
[04:50] Evan (SE): We provide a small SDK utility and examples to normalize placeholders, strip timestamps, and canonicalize clinician IDs — these are on the integrations page. We can include the script in the perf-run bundle.
[05:02] Jordan (CTO): Suppose we run the 48-hour test and it shows 35% savings with dedicated — what's next contract wise? We need a short pilot SOW and clear KPIs.
[05:12] Maya (AE): We'll draft a pilot SOW and include KPIs: p95 < 200ms for patient-chat, p99 < 350ms for summarization, and >= 30% cost reduction goal for summarization compared to current baseline. We'll include rollback and canary thresholds.
[05:26] Sam (Product): Are there any gotchas — like data residency or region-specific egress costs?
[05:31] Evan (SE): Yes, region tags drive egress and sometimes forced replication. The console flags routes with multi-region egress and gives line item attribution so you can see cross-region costs. For data residency we can pin a route to a region and limit routing.
[05:45] Priya (SRE): On observability — can we get token-level traces for a given request ID? We want to trace latency back to model step.
[05:52] Evan (SE): Yep, the tracing hook will show token-by-token timing and which kernel was used; we persist it in your account's audit logs for the configured retention. Note long retention is an add-on per the docs.
[06:05] Jordan (CTO): Any mention of competitors? we're also evaluating Sagemaker endpoints and a managed Anthropic product. How does Redwood differentiate?
[06:12] Maya (AE): Short answer: unified inference controls + the Console's per-route economics and optimization toolkit. We provide explicit levers (batching, cache, quantization presets) tied to measurable cost delta and a consistent runtime across hosted/dedicated/private. Also first-class support for rollouts and automatic fallbacks so production doesn't fall over.
[06:30] Sam (Product): Can the Console surface suggested prompts to canonicalize? like a diffs view?
[06:35] Evan (SE): Yes — the 'prompt insights' tab will show frequent variations and generate suggested normalizations, and you can export a normalization mapping. It's heuristic so you'll want to review.
[06:47] Jordan (CTO): Ok that would be very useful. Also can Redwood simulate quantization effects on output quality? we can't degrade clinical notes.
[06:55] Evan (SE): We have an Optimize module that runs lightweight evals on a held-out prompt set and shows quality vs cost curves for each quantized variant. For safety-critical text we recommend running the eval set you care about; we can include your eval prompts in the pilot.
[07:10] Priya (SRE): Who runs the pilot infra? will it be on our AWS account?
[07:14] Maya (AE): Two options: run the perf-run on Redwood-managed sandbox dedicated nodes, or spin up Redwood Private in your VPC for an on-prem style run. For the initial 48-hour we'd recommend Redwood sandbox to speed iteration. If results look good we can schedule a VPC Private deployment for the pilot phase.
[07:32] Sam (Product): What's the expected timeline to get the perf-run started?
[07:35] Evan (SE): If you provide sample traffic and authorization we can start within 3 business days. Preparing the normalization scripts and harness is usually 2-3 days.
[07:45] Jordan (CTO): Good. Priya — anything else from security?
[07:48] Priya (SRE): We'll need to see SOC2 type II reports, network architecture, and the KMS integration docs. Also want to confirm RBAC audit trail.
[07:58] Maya (AE): We'll send the SOC2 and KMS notes and schedule the security deep dive with Evan and our security engineer.
[08:05] Evan (SE): I'll include a perf-run checklist in the follow-up email: steps to anonymize or redact PHI if needed, test data format, and the harness to replay traffic.
[08:16] Jordan (CTO): One last question — can you set up alerts for cost anomalies per route?
[08:21] Evan (SE): Yes, the console supports anomaly detection; you can set thresholds or let us run a model to detect deviations from baseline. Alerts can create a ticket or trigger a scaling policy.
[08:33] Sam (Product): Great. Let's recap next steps.
[08:36] Maya (AE): Recap: we'll send pilot SOW + pricing, SOC2 and KMS docs; Evan will prepare perf-run harness and normalization scripts; Chiron will provide sample traffic and pick a 48-hour window. We'll schedule security deep dive week of 5/25.
[08:52] Jordan (CTO): Sounds good. Thanks, everyone.
[08:55] Maya (AE): Thanks all, we'll follow up with the materials.
[09:00] (meeting ends)
notes: Customer is motivated by cost savings on long-context summarization and stable low p95 for patient-chat. Key blockers: SOC2/KMS questions, commit/contract concerns for dedicated. Pilot suggested: 48-hour perf run + Optimize evals.
risky_phrases_and_mis-transcriptions: KV cash (should be KV cache), memory thermal (mis-transcribed from memory 'stack' or 'footprint'), 'Speaker 2' mis-attributed at times, occasional run-ons and filler words present
